summary.headline: Yatra Q2 FY27 revenue from operations fell 39% YoY to INR 2,136 mn, while gross margin held flat at INR 1,255 mn and net loss was INR 7 mn.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations fell 39% YoY to INR 2,136 mn, mainly on a sharp MICE decline (gross bookings down ~63% YoY) after an unusually strong prior-year quarter. Gross margin (revenue less service costs) was flat YoY at INR 1,255 mn, supported by air and standalone hotels, while adjusted EBITDA fell 41% to INR 150 mn and the company posted a net loss of INR 7 mn. Management said air gross bookings grew 15% YoY, air margin rose to 4.4% of bookings, and MICE grew ~37% QoQ. Other expenses rose on affiliate commissions, which management described as a short-term measure, and no formal annual guidance was given.

segments.name: Air ticketing
segments.commentary: Q2 passenger volume 1.298 mn (-2% YoY) versus domestic industry -6%; gross bookings +15% YoY to INR 17,060 mn; gross margin +29% YoY to INR 757 mn at 4.4% of bookings. Management said air outperformed the market and volumes rose ~4% QoQ against an industry fall of ~15%.

segments.name: Standalone hotels
segments.commentary: Gross bookings grew ~20% YoY per management, driven by supply expansion and distribution; management described growth as independent of MICE.

segments.name: Hotels and packages (reported)
segments.commentary: Q2 gross bookings -21% YoY to INR 4,054 mn and gross margin -34% YoY to INR 299 mn (7.37% of bookings vs 8.86%), reflecting MICE weakness. H1 gross margin INR 684 mn, -11% YoY.

segments.name: MICE
segments.commentary: Gross bookings down ~63% YoY against a very large prior-year international quarter, but up ~37% QoQ. Management accepted lower margins to retain large customers and rebuild volumes; Middle East exposure is ~35-40% of international travel and still muted ~15-20%.

segments.name: Corporate travel
segments.commentary: Corporate gross bookings +18% YoY; ~54% of existing customers expanded spend and 177 new corporate customers went live. Travel Pro (mid-market/SME) secured 30+ customers with ~INR 825 mn estimated annual potential; RECAP has 25 wins, 8 live.

segments.name: Kanu (international partnership)
segments.commentary: Only ~1.5 months of execution in Q2, managing ~30% of the corporate business in the region; now contributing positively at operating level and expected to improve in coming quarters.

guidance_outlook: No formal full-year guidance given; management referred to the earlier medium-term margin guidance as still applicable.
Management expects H2 FY27 to improve on H1 across air, hotels and MICE, with Q4 expected to be materially better.
About 60% of the cost base is fixed; management said roughly 60% of incremental revenue should flow to bottom line as business recovers at the same mix.
Other expenses expected to taper by INR 3-4 mn in coming quarters; normalised run-rate of ~INR 47-48 mn cited by management.
Debt expected to reduce materially in the current quarter as idle cash from IPO-related proceeds is deployed, with full benefit in the following quarter.
Management indicated margins to be around 10% of gross margin for the period, lower than last year, with operating leverage to lift margins as volumes return.
capex_capacity: Technology investments continued through GCP; INR 52 mn of costs incurred in Q2 on growth initiatives (Kanu, RECAP, Travel Pro).
Operating headcount efficiency improved ~5% YoY despite growing transaction volumes, with AI-assisted chats up ~25% QoQ and chat-based cancellations up 67%.
Implementation timelines: elite corporate clients ~1.5 months; mid-market/SME now under two weeks, down from about a month.
Travel Pro adding 30-35 new logos per quarter with ~INR 80 mn plus annual travel potential per cohort (as stated on the call).
demand_pricing: Domestic air passenger traffic down ~6% YoY and ~15% QoQ; international traffic for Indian carriers down ~19% YoY; airfares up ~20% per management.
MICE customers shifted to smaller programs and deferred budgets; company chose to price more aggressively to retain relationships, so volume rose but margins lagged.
Receivables rose to INR 610 mn at Sep 2026 from INR 335 mn at Mar 2026 (as stated), attributed to corporate business growth; management said DSO is not materially changed.
Affiliate channel scaled, adding ~INR 121 mn of incremental commission cost, which sits in other expenses rather than gross margin; management said it is a short-term measure.

qa_highlights.question: Why was sequential gross margin growth only ~2% despite MICE improvement and Kanu revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it priced MICE more flexibly to rebuild volumes, so margins lagged volume; Kanu had only ~1.5 months of execution in Q2 and should improve in later quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the YoY rise in other expenses and will it persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Affiliate commissions drove ~INR 13 mn of the ~INR 15 mn increase; management called it short-term to protect airline commission slabs and expects some tapering, with normalised other expenses around INR 47-48 mn.

qa_highlights.question: Why has debt increased and how will it reduce?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower MICE advances reduced customer float; management expects material debt reduction in the current quarter as idle cash is deployed, with full benefit next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the H2 outlook versus H1 and last year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects H2 to be significantly better than H1, with MICE order book improving quarter on quarter and air/hotels trending to plan; no formal full-year guidance.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the air margin is driven by affiliate expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the affiliate cost increase covers both air and hotels, and after adjusting for it the underlying air margin still shows about 25 bps YoY improvement from better negotiation.

qa_highlights.question: Is Middle East exposure hurting the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Middle East was about 35-40% of international travel and is still muted by ~15-20%; corporate traffic has shifted to direct Europe and US routes.

risks_watch: MICE margin pressure from discounting to retain customers; recovery in margins is management's stated expectation but not yet visible.
Working capital: receivables up sharply and debt up over three quarters; trajectory of debt reduction after IPO-related cash deployment.
Affiliate commission costs elevated in other expenses; watch whether they taper as management guided.
Industry consolidation: smaller B2B players squeezed by working-capital needs, which could benefit Yatra but depends on macro recovery.
Pending corporate card and a proposed West Coast-related corporate process (timing not committed) are open items; management could not guide on completion within this financial year.
summary.management_tone: Cautious on the near-term macro and MICE, but confident on air outperformance, corporate growth and H2 recovery. Management was candid about accepting lower MICE margins for volume, and somewhat evasive on timing for the corporate card and the West Coast process, and declined formal annual guidance.

growth.why: No formal full-year guidance was given and the FY27 margin guide was withdrawn; management expects H2 to improve on H1 and Q4 to be materially better, backed only by qualitative air share gains, MICE volume recovery, Travel Pro/RECAP wins and a 60% incremental flow-through, with no specific capacity or contracted orders quantified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Adjusted EBITDA margin was 11.96% of gross margin in Q2 (down 41% YoY) and management guided only to around 10% for the period; ~60% incremental flow-through and Kanu/MICE recovery could lift margins, but MICE is being priced aggressively to retain volume and the affiliate commission (~INR 121 mn) sits in other expenses.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.when: H2 FY27, Q4 FY27 materially better
rows.why: Air passenger volume rose ~4% QoQ against an industry fall of ~15%, corporate bookings grew 18% YoY with 177 new corporate customers live, and management expects H2 to improve on H1 across air, hotels and MICE; however, Q2 hotel room nights fell 3% YoY and total bookings were down.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex not discussed beyond INR 52 mn of technology spend in Q2 on growth initiatives, with no utilisation or new-capacity plan given; asset-light model with a net cash position of INR 2,180 mn.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No formal annual guidance was given and the prior margin guidance was dropped, while H1 revenue fell 28% YoY and Q2 revenue fell 39% YoY.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Revenue fell 39% YoY in Q2 and 28% YoY in H1, adjusted EBITDA fell 41% in Q2, and management withdrew formal full-year guidance, so any formal FY27 guide could come in below prior expectations if MICE recovery lags.

rows.label: Debt reduction as IPO cash is deployed
rows.when: current quarter (Q3 FY27), full benefit Q4 FY27
rows.why: Management expects material debt reduction this quarter as idle IPO-related cash is deployed, with cash plus term deposits at INR 2,180 mn at 30 Sep 2026, but receivables rose to INR 610 mn from INR 335 mn in March 2026.

rows.label: Other expenses taper to normalised run-rate
rows.why: Management guided other expenses to taper by INR 3-4 mn in coming quarters toward a normalised INR 47-48 mn, though affiliate commissions of about INR 121 mn remain elevated and are called short-term.

rows.label: Kanu international partnership scaling
rows.why: Kanu managed about 30% of the regional corporate business after only ~1.5 months of execution in Q2 and is now contributing positively at operating level, with management expecting improvement in coming quarters.
